notes.title: Time Hacker is now available in Early Access
notes.notes:
Time Hacker is a puzzle game in which your task is to take advantage of the time stop and use physics to take all enemies down. Blow up flammable barrels and explosive gas. Break chains, rescue hostages, dodge shots, change the direction of cars and cranes, place dynamite, shockers, and more. It’s all about creativity and ingenuity. 

Early Access includes 40 exciting levels of varying difficulty + Sandbox Mode, in which the sky is the limit on your creative destruction.

[previewyoutube=ddNymVtbtOA;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Time Hacker Development Diary I Part 4
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/35af629870b383eb06e3388561dd1ecb6b2023dc.jpg[/img]

We are finally on the home stretch! Time Hacker is coming out very soon in Early Access!

A lot has happened since our last dev diary. For eight months now we have been polishing the game towards its best possible version. For us, our games like children: you put your best into them, then (anxiously) watch with pride as they thrive in the world.

We spent a great deal of time searching for the best implementation of the game. We tested various hypotheses and looked for the best solutions. When it came to the mechanics, for example, we tried many options and performed dozens of tests. We received a lot of great feedback from the two open betas we released, so we want to say a big thank you to everyone who participated. You really helped us bring this game to where it is now!

Many of you know that as this game has developed, it’s name has changed several times. To be honest, we got a little confused ourselves! It started with the name "Revenge," then we moved on to Change Ranger, a name we thought was more descriptive. We liked Change  Ranger, but eventually we realized that it did not characterize the game accurately enough, nor could it convey the game’s atmosphere sufficiently. We listened to the community and finally settled on the perfect name for the game: “Time Hacker.” We promise, we will not change the name again! :)

Moving on, we made rather comprehensive changes to the core mechanics of the game. When you play Time Hacker now, you’ll be surprised at how different it is from the Change Ranger demo. Character posing, movement, and time freezing mechanics have all changed significantly. The result is that playing the game now feels more dangerous and exciting. The new mechanics also unlock a much greater sense of interaction with the game environment. No matter how much we describe the changes, we won't be able to convey the feeling of the game. You should try it by yourself!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/20f33a2604b2321f6c94f2a4132533fa98a9574d.gif[/img]

In terms of the in-game characters, we’ve replaced the original human-like characters with more ambiguous gold and aluminium colored bots. We’ve done this to ensure the game remains free of potential discriminatory insinuations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/0015722ba8269a46c66b639343aa9f0df3b24525.png[/img]

However, please rest assured that the enemies are still very realistic in their own way. To achieve this, we recorded motion-capture character animations. Enemies will attack you dynamically and relentlessly. Here’s a video demonstration:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/f2f5ede8af59e8b519bb3081365df2edd4bf1d1f.gif[/img]

For the Early Access release, we have not yet managed to integrate a storyline for the game. We have, however, included bits and pieces of plot background in the hopes you will speculate on what is to come. We plan to integrate a complete storyline for the Full Release. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/eac00bb4853b2b4880e91cfeab34706eeee18958.gif[/img]

As for the structure of the game, we’ve redesigned the logic of the levels and divided the scenes into splints, easy levels, and difficult levels. Obviously, the difficulty of the levels will increase as you progress through the game. You will have to come up with more and more sophisticated methods of making it to the next level. You will definitely need to be clever!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/792edbac92a5a8176b98fce988896941f440ad1b.png[/img]

We are now in the final stages of development! We're currently working on sounds, menu interfaces, and a final polishing of the levels.

This project means a lot to us. We put a great deal of effort into the creation of Time Hacker and we hope that as you play the game, you will be able to feel the love we put into it.

Thank you,
Joy Way Team

notes.title: Change Ranger Dev Diary Part 3: a behind-the-scenes look at VR game development
notes.notes:
Hi, my name is [b]Aidar [/b]and I am the lead game designer for [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1216350/Change_Ranger_VR/][b]Change Ranger. [/b][/url]Today I would like to tell you my personal origin story, where the idea for [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1216350/Change_Ranger_VR/]Change Ranger[/url][/b] came from, and how our team is developing the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/258e38e231cec0f23d8068b0891f41e93bd9ea52.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]My origin[/b][/h1]

You might say my path to becoming a VR game developer is typical. As a child, I liked to draw 2D cartoon characters, and I dreamed of becoming a cartoonist. Later, with the advent of computers, I became acquainted with 3D modeling and 3D animation. Designing in 3D brought, pardon the pun, another dimension to my art, and it quickly consumed a lot of my time. But it was when I discovered programming that I really got sucked into my computer. By age 12 I was spending all my free time in front of the screen building simple games and prototypes. With my characters now animated, they were that much more real, and it was that much more fun. You can probably see where this is going, right? From 2D, to 3D, to moving characters: the logical progression of course leads to virtual reality. So now — and I have to say I feel like the luckiest guy in the world — I’m fulfilling my childhood dream. The best part is I get to “work” in the coolest, most immersive, most realistic medium there is: VR!

[h1][b]The Change Ranger Concept[/b][/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/d74136b643f94f276f642fed002751496d6ca223.gif[/img]

My inspiration for the game came partly from the X-Men character Mercury and the DC character Flash. I thought, wouldn’t it be cool if we could have the powers of those characters like stopping time, controlling the bodies of others while they’re “frozen”, redirecting bullets, and so on. Secondly, and here I drew inspiration from games like Super Hot VR, I wanted the player to be able to experience cool sensations like evading bullets. I really wanted the game to leverage the advantages brought by the VR medium. Thirdly, I wanted to add an element of thinking. This is why Change Ranger forces the player to solve a sort of puzzle in order to complete each level in the most creatively and funniest way. I know from my personal VR gaming experiences that it’s fun to play in the company of friends. This game uses humor as a way to make group play more enjoyable.

[h1][b]Behind the Scenes at Change Ranger[/b][/h1]

I proposed the idea for [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1216350/Change_Ranger_VR/]Change Ranger[/url][/b] and oversaw the building of an initial prototype. At first it was called “Revenge” and was published on itch.io where it proved to be a very popular game. It was downloaded a lot and some bloggers even made videos (shout out to the channels Ben plays VR, Ctop, and everyone else who supported the game!).

There are currently six talented and dedicated people working on the game (plus me). Our team consists of two programmers (Zagit and Irek), one artist (Anton), one level artist (Igor), one level designer (Vlad), one screenwriter (Alex) and one game designer (me).

The development process is as follows:
[list]
[*] [b]Alex [/b] writes the cutscene script and the content of the comics.
[*] [b]Anton[/b] makes the character design and draws the comics.
[*] [b]Irek[/b] writes the main architecture of the game.
[*] [b]Vlad[/b] creates the test environment and arranges the characters.
[*] [b]Igor [/b]sews the environment.
[*] [b]Zagit[/b] collects and tests the levels.
[*] I oversee the general process, help out where I can, and sometimes create and test mechanics.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/8cf7c7450f91558d32d390960c0d1bd15168dfe4.png[/img]

When we reach a certain stage of the game, we try to demonstrate it to the players. So, for example, our team created a prototype first, and then the first demo version. We collected feedback and made edits. Now, the second demo version is being prepared (tentatively to be released at the end of March).

Despite the fact that we are a small indie studio, I, like any developer, really hope that Change Ranger will appeal to a large number of VR players and will leave its mark as something new and interesting for the VR community. Our team is working hard to reach that goal. We are also very grateful to everyone who has written their opinion on this game. Your feedback has been incredibly valuable to the development process.

While we have set the release date for the game at the end of April, we have of course been deluged with numerous setbacks. Challenges we’re overcoming include the complexity of developing player and character mechanics, script docking, and so on. We also need to integrate feedback from the VR community, which of course takes additional time. We are doing our best to complete the game on schedule, but our priority remains releasing the highest-quality, most complete game possible.

Thanks to all,

Please join our communities, keep up the awesome feedback, and stay safe!

notes.title: Change Ranger: Development Diary I Part 2
notes.notes:
Hey guys,

This is the second installment in our Dev Diary for [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1216350/Change_Ranger_VR/]Change Ranger[/url]. You can read the first installment [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1216350/announcements/detail/3968171431178390664]here[/url].

The game itself, as many have already noticed, is built on the Unity engine. This is great for small teams like ours. I would like to name a specific version of Unity that we’re using, but we change them quite often to keep up with the times.

Unity makes it easy to use, for example, NVIDIA PhysX to calculate physics. It also makes it easy to integrate Final IK, which is responsible for many animations.

Getting down to our progress for the week. Here’s what we worked on last week:

1. We mapped out the core of the plot and we decided on the majority of the main characters. Now, in addition to the fantastically entertaining gore, there is a real sense why it’s all happening.  We promise the story and the characters will help to bring the game alive for you. Are you intrigued yet?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/480471b25fa06c71204afa7fa985717da61b6ebf.jpg[/img]

2. The game is divided into four main sections. Each section consists of several levels or “scenes”. Each section will culminate in a boss, who can be found in the final level. The boss is a unique enemy character who will have his own special ability or abilities, making him more difficult to defeat. Fighting the bosses will be more challenging, but also more fun. 

3. In total, we’ve already planned approximately 40-50 levels. As we build the levels we are also expanding the plot. As you progress through the levels, you’ll be drawn deeper into the plot and you’ll come across unexpected twists and turns. There will also be more complicated mechanics as you progress through the game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/f9e3f2d62fc4ae4ecd981492d0ec2bc2ef33c5f7.jpg[/img]

The huge second location is divided into two parts. We are already working on creating additional levels for the second and third parts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/f052295a209138f83f20aa4485e974229949e865.jpg[/img]

4. We’re continuing work on the basic mechanics and assessment mechanism for passing each level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/421454b39bd14e74864af1933932122137956744.jpg[/img]


We are introducing new and interesting mechanics. For example, you will be able to choose by yourself when to stop time. You’ll also  have the ability to rewind time when you fail. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/d28efafebf9afe899756e904dd4be22d626caf8d.gif[/img]

5. As mentioned in our first Dev Diary instalment, we’ve been working to optimize the graphics for the first 11 levels. We’re happy to report that we’ve managed to complete that work already. Here’s a before and after:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/cab3cefdfafa05f8eeb14575be1c40de558fc5f9.jpg[/img]

Thank you again and please keep up your awesome feedback!

Stay tuned for our next post!

notes.title: Change Ranger: Development Diary I Part 1
notes.notes:
Hey guys ,

As you know we’ve released demos for two of our new games: [b]“Change Ranger”[/b] and [b]“Brain VS Zombies”.[/b] Based on the reaction of the community we have decided to concentrate on Change Ranger for now. It seems most of you liked that demo more, so, with a lot of work from our team, it looks like Change Ranger has a better chance of evolving into a really great game.

If you haven't tried Change Ranger yet, you can download the demo on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1216350/Change_Ranger/]Steam[/url] for free.

Thank you to everyone who has taken the time to comment. We’ve been carefully considering your very helpful feedback and our developers are working hard to improve the game based on what you’ve said.

We are starting a [b]“Development Diary” [/b] to share with you the progress we’re making on Change Ranger and we’d love to get more feedback from you along the way.

So let’s start! Here’s what we’ve done since the last release:

[olist]
[*] We’ve designed six new levels for the first location. This means there are now 11 levels in the first location. We are now working to optimize these first levels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/cf130bb347a67457916d898e7dd426bf8c086279.png[/img]

[*] We designed a huge second location. This new location encompasses scenes from a city including a power plant, construction sites, a railway station, an airport, gas stations, and more. Encounter gangsters in unexpected places as you explore a complete city environment in VR.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/bc275f690d2a3693c4f9f1ed9bfb1b5bc9f15181.jpg[/img]

[*] Ideas for new levels were collected from the feedback of those who played the demo, which included community members, game designers, and university students. We’d love more feedback on this. If you have ideas for locations you’d like to see included, please leave a comment on[url=https://www.reddit.com/r/JoyWay/] Reddit [/url]or in our [url=https://discord.gg/y9wXxGs]Discord server[/url].

[*] Primary and secondary mechanics are being improved. Primary mechanics refer to superhero control, inverse kinematics, ghost movement, and the process of “possessing” bad guys. Secondary mechanics refer to movements like aiming and types of shots by type of weapon. We started processing scripts to help automate basic tasks in the level creation process but we’re still working through some challenges there. Feels like some of these low-life gangsters are trying to sabotage our master plan. No stress though, with powers like ours, we all know who will win that battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/587a9449c51eeb109b69661419c52647797597f5.png[/img]

[*] An assessment for passing each level will be introduced with higher scores given for cleverly killing gangsters in more unique ways. You’re basically God here, so when you warp in to ambush five gangsters, show some respect and kill with a little style -- and wrap up some points while you’re at it. Possessing one or two of these simpletons, aiming their guns at each other, then sitting back as they blow each others’ brains out is fun -- but it gets old fast. So figure out new ways to reign down death - like maybe blow up some gas cylinders such so the shrapnel takes out the majority of the criminals, then leave just one of those morons to blow his own brains out.

[*] We added a tonne of customizations. Now the bad guys are regaled with a wide assortment of distinguishing accessories. We figure baddies with glasses, beards, afros, and... pylons offer more narrative and comedic potential.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36605925/066102d63017d2b902c4fac0fba4d4aa70591d24.jpg[/img]

[*] We’ve hired a screenwriter to work on the narrative of the game. Our aim is to sharpen up the backstory so the game’s narrative makes sense and is more engaging. You’ll find out details like who our hero is, where he came from, what his mission is, and why all these gangstas need to kill each other.
[/olist]

We plan to report on the status of development weekly to get more feedback from you. So stay tuned for updates!

notes.title: “Change Ranger” VR released today. Try the demo on Steam now!
notes.notes:
We are excited to announce the release of our “Change Ranger” demo, available on Steam...and it’s absolutely FREE!

[previewyoutube=A4khImHTBpY;full][/previewyoutube]

Hack time in VR with “Change Ranger,” the game where time stops just long enough for you to cleverly sabotage criminals. Redirect their guns, reposition deadly objects and otherwise rearrange the scene to trigger your enemies’ downfall. Then, the second time flow is restored to normal, sit back and revel in the chaos as the criminals are destroyed. Watch out though because if your changes weren’t enough to polish off all your enemies, they’ll be out for revenge.

The full version will be out in March!

Enjoy the demo and leave your feedback in our communities:
